h1: The 6 Best Poly Garden Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Poly Garden Carts 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six poly garden dump carts compared on capacity, wheel type and handle design, from light-duty wagons to 1200 lb haulers.
summary: The BILT HARD 1,200 lb poly dump cart is the best poly garden cart: a confirmed poly 7 cubic foot bed, no-flat tires and a convertible handle. The smaller BILT HARD 600 lb with a rotating handle suits tight spaces, and the VEVOR is the cheapest confirmed poly. The CAMMOO carts need their bed material checked.
intro: Capacity is the number everyone reads and the one that tells you least. A 1,200 lb rating is meaningless if the bed flexes, the axle is thin or the cart is too wide to pass through your garden gate. Poly beds earn their place because they do not rust or dent and they shed wet soil, but they are not all built to the same standard.

We reviewed six dump-style carts and ranked them on spec sheets and listing details: stated capacity, bed volume, wheel and tire type, handle design and how clearly the bed material is confirmed. Four carts explicitly list a poly bed. Two others are included because their capacity is strong, with a clear note to verify the bed material before you order.

products.name: BILT HARD Poly Garden Dump Cart 1200 lbs with No Flat Tires, Quick Release, 2-in-1 Convertible Handle, 7 Cu Ft
products.verdict: The biggest confirmed poly bed in the group, built for real bulk hauling.
products.description:
The BILT HARD 1,200 lb cart has a confirmed poly bed of 7 cubic feet, no-flat tires, a quick-release feature and a handle that converts between pull and push. Seven cubic feet is the largest confirmed poly bed here, and a convertible handle lets you steer in tight spaces or haul over distance.

It ranks first because capacity, bed size and tire type are all confirmed. The 600 lb carts are lighter, and the CAMMOO 900 lb does not confirm its bed.

Buy it for moving mulch, soil or stone in large volumes. The caveats are that it is bulky to store and the priciest poly option. Skip it if your garden has narrow gates or you only haul light loads.
pros: Highest capacity of any poly cart
products.idealFor: Homeowners who move mulch, soil or stone in large volumes.
products.skipIf: Your garden has narrow gates or you only haul light loads.

products.name: BILT HARD 4 Cu.Ft. 10" No-Flat Tires Poly Yard Dump Cart with 180° Rotating Handle, 600 lbs Capacity
products.verdict: A compact poly cart whose swivelling handle makes turns easier.
products.description:
The compact BILT HARD has a 4 cubic foot confirmed poly bed, 10 inch no-flat tires, a 600 lb rating and a 180 degree rotating handle. A rotating handle makes turns easier around raised beds and narrow paths, where a fixed handle fights you.

It ranks second because the bed is smaller than the top pick, so bulk loads take more trips. It costs less.

Buy it for working around raised beds and narrow paths. Skip it if you need to move yards of material quickly. A 600 lb rating is ample for mulch and potting mix, and ten inch tires roll over roots without jarring your wrists. Because the bed holds four cubic feet, expect two or three trips for a typical mulch delivery, and keep loads even for steady handling.
products.idealFor: Gardeners working around raised beds and narrow paths.
products.skipIf: You need to move yards of material quickly.

products.name: VEVOR Poly Garden Dump Cart 4 Cu.Ft. 600 lbs 4 Wheel Wheelbarrow Dump Wagon
products.verdict: The cheapest way to get a confirmed poly bed with a 600 lb rating.
products.description:
The VEVOR dump cart has a poly bed of 4 cubic feet, four wheels, a 600 lb rating and a dump function. Four wheels keep the cart upright without help, which is steadier for people who hate tipping.

It ranks third because the tire type is not specified and the handle is plain. It is the cheapest confirmed poly bed in the group.

Buy it for a stable poly dump wagon on a budget. Skip it if you want puncture-proof tires confirmed. Check the tire description before ordering, because a cart with unknown tires may puncture on thorns or ride hard. The four-wheel layout means the cart stands upright when parked, which helps when you are loading it, and the dump latch lets you unload without lifting.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a stable poly dump wagon.
products.skipIf: You want puncture-proof tires confirmed in the listing.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Poly Dump Cart, 2-Wheel Garden Wagon, 4 Cu Ft, 300lb Capacity
products.verdict: A familiar name for light loads, with half the rating of its rivals.
products.description:
The Gorilla Carts poly dump cart has a 4 cubic foot bed, a 300 lb capacity and two wheels. It is an established garden cart brand, and two wheels pivot easily for turns.

It ranks fourth because the 300 lb rating gives less headroom for wet soil. It has half the rating of its rivals.

Buy it for light yard work like leaves, potting mix and tools. Skip it if you haul stone, wet soil or heavy bagged material. Fill the bed carefully, since 4 cubic feet of wet soil can exceed 300 lb. The two-wheel pivot is easy on turns, and the brand's reputation helps with parts. Treat it as a light-duty cart, not a bulk hauler.
products.idealFor: Light yard work like leaves, potting mix and tools.
products.skipIf: You haul stone, wet soil or heavy bagged material.

The CAMMOO 900 lb dump cart has 10 inch no-flat tires and a dump wagon design. A 900 lb rating sits between the 600 and 1,200 lb options, and 10 inch wheels roll over roots well.

whatMatters.detail: A poly bed is molded plastic that will not rust, rot or dent the way a steel tray can. It matters because garden carts live outdoors and sit wet. Look for the word poly or polyethylene in the title or bullet points, not just a vague mention of heavy duty. The BILT HARD, VEVOR and Gorilla carts confirm it, and the CAMMOO listings do not.

Capacity is the weight the frame is rated for, while bed volume in cubic feet is how much material fits. Wet soil and gravel weigh far more per cubic foot than mulch, so a big bed with a low rating can overload fast. Compare both numbers on the listing before you decide, and remember that the Gorilla cart's 4 cubic feet is rated for only 300 lb.

No-flat tires are solid or foam-filled and cannot puncture on thorns or nails. They ride firmer than air tires but need no maintenance. Check whether the listing says no-flat explicitly, and note the wheel diameter, since bigger wheels roll over roots more easily. The BILT HARD and CAMMOO carts list no-flat, and the VEVOR does not state the tire type.

Two-wheel carts pivot and tip easily, while four-wheel wagons stay upright by themselves. The choice affects stability under heavy loads and how well the cart turns. Look at the wheel layout in the product images to see which style you are buying. The VEVOR has four wheels, and the Gorilla two.

A fixed handle is simple, but a rotating or convertible handle can change how you steer and store the cart. It helps in tight beds and narrow gates. Check the listing for words like rotating, convertible or quick release to see what is offered. The BILT HARD carts list these features, while the others show plain handles.

faq.q: Is a poly bed better than steel?
faq.a: Poly will not rust or dent and sheds wet soil easily. Steel can be stiffer under sharp loads, but needs paint care. For most home gardens poly is the lower-maintenance choice, especially for mulch and compost.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying a garden cart?
faq.a: Shopping by capacity alone. Check bed volume, wheel type and whether the cart fits through your gates, since a huge cart that cannot reach the beds is useless. Measure the narrowest gate before ordering the BILT HARD 1,200 lb.

faq.q: Is the 1200 lb cart worth it over a 600 lb one?
faq.a: Only if you move heavy material often. For mulch and potting mix, a 600 lb cart like the BILT HARD rotating-handle model is more than enough, and it stores more easily than the 7 cubic foot cart.
Most dump carts ship partly assembled and need wheels, axle and handle fitted. Plan for basic hand tools and read the listing for what is included, and set aside about an hour for the larger cart.

faq.q: How do I maintain a poly cart?
faq.a: Rinse the bed after wet or acidic loads, keep the dump latch clear of dirt and check axle fasteners now and then. Store it out of constant direct sun to protect the plastic.

faq.q: What about the CAMMOO carts with no stated bed material?
faq.a: Ask the seller or check the product images before ordering. If the bed is not plastic, a poly-specific cart like the VEVOR is the safer buy, since a steel bed rusts where poly does not.

finalTake: The BILT HARD 1,200 lb is the right poly cart for most gardeners who haul in bulk, thanks to its confirmed poly bed and no-flat tires. Pick the smaller BILT HARD for tight spaces and the VEVOR for a cheap confirmed poly. Verify the bed material on any unlisted model.
